messages:
nina (People Ops): Quick question 1: employee relocated from US -> UK mid-year and we also did a payroll provider cutover. They stopped 401(k) and HSA deductions when they moved. Need to confirm if we can: 1) remit missed employer match for periods when deferrals occurred, 2) treat catch-up (50+) for partial-year, and 3) any vendor/legal blockers for a retro payment across the cutover.
jordan (Payroll): Can you share exact dates? cutover date + relocation effective date + last US pay? That determines remittance windows.
nina (People Ops): Relocation effective 2025-08-20, last US pay 2025-08-28 (paid), payroll cutover 2025-09-10. Employee turned 50 on 2025-06-02.
jordan (Payroll): Ok. Vendor note: old 401k provider accepts retro employee and employer contributions up to 90 days after plan quarter close if we request a cutoff exception. After our vendor cutover there is a reconciliation period but we can still push a manual match if we provide signed employee authorization + payroll export.
mike (Finance): From tax/accounting side: employer match is an employer expense for the period when deferrals were made. We should record on the month the match is remitted, but attach memo referencing the eligible pay periods. Also check whether the match triggers US tax reporting for the employee if they're now UK tax resident  legal will need to advise.
benefits-bot: Policy snippet: "Employer match is computed on elective deferrals actually remitted to the plan during the plan year. Catch-up contributions permitted per IRS rules; plan doc governs election timing. For cutover remittances, contact payroll@redwood with documentation." <https://docs.redwood.com/benefits/401k-manual-remit>
nina (People Ops): Action items I think: - collect pay export for 2025-01-01 -> 2025-08-28 showing elective deferrals and catch-up withheld - get employee to sign authorization for manual employer match remittance - finance to create remittance and GL code
jordan (Payroll): Agreed. Also need ssn_last4 and legacy payroll id for vendor. If we miss the local cutoff I'll escalate to vendor ops.
emma (Employee): Hi team 1: I'm happy to sign whatever you need. Do I get to contribute catch-up for the full year even though I left mid-year? I wasn't sure if that prorates.
mike (Finance): You can only contribute catch-up up to the amount actually withheld on US payroll. The plan's catch-up limit is annual, but we cannot retroactively withhold amounts that weren't elected. If you want to maximize catch-up you'd have had to elect it earlier.
nina (People Ops): To be explicit: if you elected catch-up prior to move and deferrals were withheld, we'll remit those. We can't add extra catch-up that wasn't withheld. We'll confirm amounts and share a summary before asking you to sign.
emma (Employee): Got it, thanks. Please confirm estimate so I can sign.
nina (People Ops): Preliminary numbers from payroll export: employee elective deferrals (pre-tax) Jan-Aug = $11,400; catch-up withheld = $2,000; estimated company match (4% on eligible wages) = $2,160 (estimate). Jordan will confirm final.
jordan (Payroll): Confirming I can submit a manual match request to legacy vendor once we have: signed authorization PDF, payroll export CSV, ssn_last4, legacy payroll id, remittance file from finance. I'll open vendor ticket today (ref: TKT-401K-REM-2114).
mike (Finance): Finance ready to fund remittance GL 6500. Send estimate now and final invoice later. Also note: we should cc legal if vendor flags cross-border withholding or treaty concerns.
benefits-bot: Reminder: submit requests using the 401k manual remit template: https://docs.redwood.com/benefits/forms/manual-remit-template.xlsx
nina (People Ops): Perfect. I'll collect docs and post back. Thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
